extracted.intended_audience: users of Isabelle/Isar (proof engineers, researchers, and advanced students writing formal proofs in Isabelle/HOL)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and conventions for writing structured, human-readable proofs in the Isabelle/Isar proof language (Isabelle/Pure and object-logics such as Isabelle/HOL). Covers proof block structure, context elements, elimination/case rules, calculational chains, and proof-method usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use have/show for intermediate and final claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Use have to state intermediate goals and show to refine pending subgoals; have states an intermediate goal and show refines a pending subgoal (often inside a nested proof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "have A ∧ B ...", "show B". The two dots ".." refer to a complete proof using indicated facts and a canonical rule. "have states an intermediate goal." Use show within subproofs to discharge a pending goal. The text contrasts forwards (have/then) and backwards (proof ... assume ... show ...) styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augment context with assume
rubrics_metrics.description: assume augments the proof context with a local hypothesis which may be used subsequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "assume x ∈ A and x ∈ B then have x ∈ A ∩ B ..". The default inference for assume is export (i.e. assume produces A ⟹ A locally). Use then to immediately use the assumed fact. The included inference may be used later to discharge the assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce arbitrary parameters with fix
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare arbitrary-but-fixed local parameters using fix x :: α; in exported results x may become any term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "fix a assume a ∈ A show x ∈ a ... q.e.d." The exported result from a block with fix becomes a universally quantified rule, e.g. (λx. ...). Use fix in nested subproofs for backward-style proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured subproofs with proof ... qed
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a nested proof block (proof ... qed) to create local contexts and to derive rules that refine an outer goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical pattern: "have X proof (rule r) fix x assume ... show ?thesis qed". Subproofs implement the fix-assume-show outline. Block structure can also be indicated by { ... }. Use next to jump to the next section of a block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward reasoning and chaining with then/from/with/this
rubrics_metrics.description: Chain facts in forward style using from, then, with and the special fact this (refers to last result).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations: "from a ≡ note a then"; "with a ≡ from a and this". Example: "from ‹A› and ‹B› show C x y". Use these to feed results into subsequent steps; they interact with methods (then have ... proof (rule r)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of methods and 'by' for applying rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply proof methods to the current goal via by/method: default method is standard; rules may be applied explicitly with by (rule r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods take facts indicated by then or using. Basic methods: "-" (leave goal unchanged), "this" (apply facts as rules), "rule" (apply facts to another rule then to goal). Abbreviations: "by method1 method2" for "proof method1 qed method2"; "." is shorthand for "by this"; ".." is shorthand for "by standard".

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and use attributes on facts ([OF], [intro], [symmetric], [trans], etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts and theorems can be given attributes to modify how they are used (e.g., resolution ordering, introduction/elimination markers, symmetry/transitivity collections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "a [OF b]" composes facts according to resolution; "a [intro]" declares a fact as an introduction rule; declare transitivity rules in the context and use [symmetric] to get symmetric variants. The system will pick args from elim/dest/intro lists when method arguments are omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalized elimination and case rules format
rubrics_metrics.description: Elimination rules are structured with a prefix of assumptions (major premises) and one or more cases, each enabling the main conclusion in an augmented context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical names: exE (local parameter), conjE (local premises), disjE (split into cases). The general scheme: prefix assumptions, then case rules like ((λx y. B1 x y ⇒ C1 x y ⇒ R) ⇒ ...), then R as main conclusion. Use proof (rule r) to apply such eliminations, producing subproofs for each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cases/case-splitting via cases and case branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cases/case and the proof method cases to split goals into named branches and work inside each branch with the augmented local context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "proof (cases x = y rule: tertium_non_datur) ... case T ... next case F ... q.e.d.". The method cases recovers structure in a sub-proof; use next to move between cases. Isar also supports datatype-derived cases (proof (cases x)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use obtain/obtains for elimination and to inline cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use obtain to inline a single case branch into Isar text and to conservatively extend the local context with parameters and assumptions; use obtains in top-level statements to define multi-branch elimination theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern: "then obtain A where x ∈ A and A ∈ A ..". Semantics: obtain proves ((λx. A x ⇒ thesis) ⇒ thesis) and then introduces a local fixed parameter and assumptions. Important constraint: "Conclusions from this context may not mention x again!" (i.e., obtained local parameters cannot be referenced outside the scope). obtains at the statement level represents multi-case elimination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exporting results from local blocks with note
rubrics_metrics.description: Use note to export the result of a local block as a fact available in the outer context (often universally quantified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: after { fix x have B x ... } note ‹(λx. B x)› exports the local proof as a general fact; similarly define x where x ≡ a exports the expanded form. Note is how Isar indicates exported results from nested proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured theorem statements (fixes / assumes / shows / obtains)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the outer structure of theorems using fixes, assumes, shows (and obtains) to lay out local context elements and conclusions explicitly for clearer proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canonical pattern: "fixes x and y assumes A x and B y shows C x y" then proof uses local facts directly. For obtains: "obtains x and y where A x and B y" specifies multi-branch elimination rules. Presenting statements in this open format simplifies subsequent proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-machine model: alternate forward/backward modes and use of next
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that Isar/VM alternates modes between forward (state) and backward (prove) reasoning; next closes an implicit block and opens another section (not tied to subgoals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State mode accepts fix/assume/have/show. A goal statement switches to prove mode to refine the problem. Qed returns to the outer state mode. Use next to separate block sections; there is no direct connection to subgoals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the special abbreviations '.' and '..' in terminal proof steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Use '.' as shorthand for 'by this' and '..' as shorthand for 'by standard' to conclude proof steps concisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "have x ∈ A ∩ B .." uses standard method; "assume ... then show ⊥ ..". Use these for concise forward-style finishing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculational reasoning with also / finally / calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the calculational mechanism for chains of transitivity: start with also (sets calculation to current result), chain also ... have ... updates calculation via trans rules, and finish with finally to expose the final result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canonical pattern: "have a = b ... also have ... = c ... also have ... = d ... finally have a = d ." The literal ellipsis '...'(". . .") refers to the right-hand side of the previous statement. Declare appropriate trans rules in the context; Isar will combine calculation and this. Use symmetry rules or simp-based unfolding as appropriate. Avoid over-reliance on ad-hoc substitution—prefer Simp or proper transitivity setup when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and use primitive inferences and derived rules sensibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize primitive introduction/elimination rules of the object-logic (e.g., conjI, conjD1/D2, IntI, InterI) and derive convenient combined rules (conjE) for practical proof use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: derive a simultaneous elimination conjE from conjD1 and conjD2 to avoid immediate projection decisions. Use object-logic axioms as named theorems and refer to them in proofs (by (rule IntI), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution and assumption composition via reﬁnement
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose subproofs via the reﬁnement rule: a subproof with its fix/assume/show structure must fit the pending subgoal modulo unification; assumptions may be a subset of subgoal premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isar uses a combined reﬁnement inference (composition of resolution and assumption). This allows re-ordering of parameters and omission of unused context elements; subproofs need only fit modulo unification, offering flexibility in structuring proofs for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use elimination rules that introduce local parameters carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Elimination rules that introduce local parameters (e.g., exE) require nested subproofs with parameters and assumptions; alternatively use obtain to perform the same elimination more conveniently in forward style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "assume x ∈ (⋃) A then have C proof fix A assume x ∈ A and A ∈ A show C qed". The obtain form simplifies this: "then obtain A where x ∈ A and A ∈ A .." The rule involved is the same; choose obtain where it improves readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming facts for dual access (name and literal proposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: When you write have a: A the result becomes accessible both by the name (a) and by the literal proposition ‹A›.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lets you reference facts either by label or by proposition text. Use this to clarify intent and to feed facts into methods like [OF] or as explicit arguments to rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use unfolding and simplification methods for equational reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer using unfolding and the simplifier (simp) to normalize equational problems rather than manual substitutions where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: use "unfolding left_inv .." or "by (simp only: left_inv)" to normalize terms. The Simpliﬁer is the main automated tool for equational reasoning in Isabelle; use it rather than verbose ad-hoc replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorder and omit context elements to reflect natural flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Rearrange fix and assume declarations in the text according to the natural flow of reasoning; Isar's unification and Hereditary Harrop normal forms permit reordering and omission of unused context elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show different permutations of fix/assume orders that still discharge the same rule. This fine-tuning improves readability without changing exported meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about elimination/intro directions when necessary (intro/dest/elim attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify rules as intro/dest/elim as appropriate so automatic selection of rules by methods works as intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system picks rules declared as elim or dest first, then intro, when automatically selecting arguments for rule application. Tagging theorems with [intro], [elim], [dest] and other attributes helps automation and clarity.
